articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: The document is the 'SJAA EPHEMERIS', the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association. This specific issue is Volume 6, Number 12, corresponding to December 1995.

articles.title: Eye on the Ephemerides
articles.summary: The article details the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) schedule for December 1995 and January 1996, featuring general meetings, multiple star parties, and an observational astronomy class. Highlighted speakers include Dr. Christopher McKay discussing the search for life from Antarctica to Mars, and Lick Observatory historian Shiloh Unruh presenting a historical murder mystery. The piece also briefly mentions previous SJAA events and astronomical news like Comet Hale-Bopp and the 1997 total solar eclipse.

articles.title: Forty Years Ago this Month
articles.summary: This article, the final installment of the "Forty Years Ago" series, reflects on the December 1955 meeting of the San Jose Amateur Astronomers, marking the club's one-year anniversary. The meeting featured discussions on Mercury, the constellation Auriga, the Christmas Star, and an introduction to variable stars by various members. It also notes the club's growth from 24 members to 200 over four decades.

articles.title: Live From the Stratosphere, The Last Flight of the Kuiper Airborne Observatory
articles.summary: SJAA members participated in a star party at NASA/Ames, coinciding with the "Live From The Stratosphere" education program and the final flight of the Kuiper Airborne Observatory (KAO). The event engaged middle and high school students who interacted with KAO astronomers via television link and observed celestial objects through telescopes, culminating in the KAO's return and a tour of the aircraft. The author reflects on the KAO's significant history and the bittersweet end of an astronomical era.

articles.title: A Very Successful School Star Party
articles.summary: An amateur astronomer from Amador county, Jim Van Nuland, teamed up with the SJAA to organize a successful school star party at the Waldon West science camp for 200 5th and 6th graders. Despite short notice, six members with telescopes showcased celestial objects like Saturn, M31, and M57, providing an engaging astronomy experience for the students. The event highlighted efficient coordination and dedication from the astronomy club members.

articles.title: Slide and Equipment Night, September 1995
articles.summary: This article describes a "Slide and Equipment Night" event held in September 1995. During the gathering, participants showcased their astronomical equipment, with Ernie Piini presenting a folding refractor and Terry Kahl demonstrating the simplicity of her 8-inch Dobsonian telescope.

articles.title: Thanks
articles.summary: This article expresses gratitude to SJAA members and friends for their continuous support of the Telescope Loaner Program. Thanks to various donations, technical assistance, and labor, the program has expanded from a few older scopes to approximately 15 high-quality telescopes. It details recent projects, including an 11" f/4 Dobson telescope, and acknowledges numerous specific donations of parts, equipment, and expertise from club members.

articles.title: Correction to appendix in "How to Make a Telescope", 2nd edition
articles.summary: This article provides a correction to the BASIC/A code found in the appendix of the 2nd edition, 3rd printing of Jean Texereau's book "How to Make a Telescope." Dick Suiter, the author of the 'Advanced Capabilities' program version, identifies a specific error in lines 2370 and 2380, explaining how to renumber or relocate them for users of BASIC/A or QBASIC, respectively. He also clarifies the enhancements in his version over the original Remaklus version, which improved wavefront analysis by checking more reference curves.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: This document is a periodical publication statement for the SJAA Ephemeris, the monthly newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It confirms that the newsletter is published 12 times a year, from January through December, and includes the association's mailing address.

articles.title: ULYSSES Mission Status - 10/01/95
articles.summary: The Ulysses spacecraft successfully completed its primary mission of exploring the Sun's northern solar pole on September 29, 1995. It is now journeying back towards Jupiter's orbit, with plans to return to the Sun's vicinity for a second pass over its poles in September 2000. This extended mission, a joint NASA/ESA project, is funded and will allow scientists to study the Sun during its peak active sunspot phase with reversed magnetic polarity.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS, 11-08-1995
articles.summary: Comet activity has recently increased, with several comets experiencing outbursts. Periodic Comet Schwassmann-Wachmann 3 and Periodic Comet Honda-Mrkos-Pajdusakova are currently visible in the southern evening sky. Comet Hale-Bopp is currently behind the sun but will reappear in the morning sky in three months, with earlier reports of its dimming being false, attributed to viewing against the Milky Way.

articles.title: EPHEMERIDES
articles.summary: This document provides ephemeris data for four comets: 122P/de Vico, 73P/Schwassmann-Wachmann 3, C/1995 Q1 (Bradfield), and 45P/Honda-Mrkos-Pajdusakova. The tables list their celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), elongation from the Sun, and estimated magnitude at five-day intervals from mid-November to mid-January. This information is crucial for observers to locate and track these comets.
